info.title: WebTag API
info.description: Self-hosted, single-installation URL parsing and reading service. Submit URLs or multi-source ingest payloads, run the configured AI analyzer, and persist structured results in PostgreSQL. Public /api/* operations accept the static installation token, a browser session, or explicitly enabled anonymous access.

tags.name: feeds
tags.description: RSS/Atom subscriptions, reading state, folders, discovery, refresh scheduling, and OPML portability

tags.name: auth
tags.description: Authenticated client identity and optional HttpOnly browser-session exchange

post.description: Idempotent by URL: any existing URL returns its current link state without creating work, including failed links. Only a new URL creates and queues asynchronous parsing. Retry or forced re-analysis is explicit through POST /api/links/{link_id}/refresh. Clients that may retry after an ambiguous timeout should also send a stable Idempotency-Key for the exact same request.

Idempotent-Replay.description: Present with value `true` only when the response was served from the completed idempotency cache rather than by invoking the handler again.

get.description: Lists links filtered by collection kind and enrichment status. A plain legacy request defaults to completed reading links, preventing website cards from appearing in article readers. library_kind=reading|site explicitly selects a collection. The optional status= parameter takes pending|processing|failed|done; an explicit status query may return either collection and unresolved automatic captures. The status filter combines with tags/domain/content_type, the paired created_at range, and both pagination modes. Two optional modes override the normal list path: q= runs keyword search and url= performs an exact normalized-URL existence check.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Comma-separated enrichment statuses to include. Allowed values: pending, processing, failed, done. Omit with no library_kind to return completed reading links. Any other token returns 400.

parameters.name: library_kind
parameters.description: Final collection partition. Omit for legacy reading defaults; use explicitly in new Reader views.

parameters.name: tags
parameters.description: Comma-separated tags, AND match. Maximum 32 entries, each up to 64 bytes. Combines with q=.

parameters.name: low_confidence
parameters.description: Filter by the low-confidence flag. true returns only links whose enrichment was flagged as unreliable (the review queue); false returns only confident ones. Omit for no filter. Any other value is rejected with 422 — a typo that silently returned the unfiltered list would make the review queue look complete when it is not.

parameters.name: created_from
parameters.description: Inclusive created_at lower bound in RFC3339 format. Must be supplied together with created_before and be earlier than it. The server interprets the timestamp as an instant and never guesses a timezone. Combines with reading/status/tag/domain filters and both pagination modes.

parameters.name: created_before
parameters.description: Exclusive created_at upper bound in RFC3339 format. Must be supplied together with created_from; together they define the half-open interval [created_from, created_before). One-sided, malformed, equal, or reversed bounds return 422; omitting both remains valid.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Keyword query over title, summary, and tags. Results are ordered newest first, limited to 50, and are not paginated (page/after ignored). Blank or whitespace is treated as not supplied. Combines with status, tags, domain, and content_type. Over 512 runes returns 422.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: Exact normalized-URL existence check. Returns 0 or 1 link (single-element or empty items array), no pagination. Takes precedence over q= when both are supplied. An invalid URL returns 422.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Offset-mode page index. Ignored when after=, q= or url= is set.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Cursor token from the previous response's next_cursor field. Pass an empty value to start a cursor-paginated stream from the most recent link. Ignored when q= or url= is set.

post.description: Queues a fresh analysis for a link. Works for terminal links in both done and failed states — calling refresh on a failed link transitions it back to pending and clears its error (this is how the extension's failed-link retry works). Subject to a per-link cooldown (default 60s); a follow-up within the window returns 429 with a Retry-After header. For a link already pending or processing, its current asynchronous state is returned as-is (202) instead of creating duplicate work.

get.description: Returns the already-saved original body for a link without ever fetching the page. The reader keeps the original collapsed by default and calls this only when the user expands it, so opening an article does not transfer the whole body. 404 when the link is unknown or nothing has been saved yet.

post.summary: Fetch and save a link's original content
post.description: Saves original content on demand, decoupled from tagging. content is always the canonical plain-text projection used by search/indexing; content_document optionally preserves reading structure and content_format explicitly declares plain, markdown, or html. The operation is idempotent: already-saved content is returned without fetching again. Browser/text ingests prefer their stored sanitized HTML snapshot and fall back to readable text. Plain URL links use the local fetcher chain once. A fetch failure, search-summary fallback, or empty body returns 502.

put.summary: Refetch and replace a link's saved original content
put.description: Explicitly replaces the saved content snapshot for the current completed source revision. Historic browser captures without structured HTML first attempt a live URL refetch, then honestly fall back to their captured plain text if the remote page is unavailable. Unlike POST, this operation does not return the existing value without fetching.

patch.summary: Edit a link's saved original content
patch.description: Replaces the already-saved original snapshot from caller-provided source text without fetching the remote page. Markdown and other structured snapshots are normalized through the same content document sanitizer as fetched content; plain snapshots remain plain. The request must include the observed content_revision. A stale revision returns 409 content_revision_conflict, an empty normalized document returns 400 content_empty, and content over 2 MiB after JSON decoding (measured as UTF-8 bytes) returns 413 content_too_large. Failed requests preserve the existing snapshot.

200.description: Edited; the response carries content_source=user and the post-write content_revision.

400.description: Invalid link ID or content_empty after normalization (error_code=content_empty).

409.description: Link is not editable or the observed saved-content generation is stale (error_code=content_revision_conflict).

413.description: Decoded content exceeds 2 MiB UTF-8 bytes (error_code=content_too_large).

post.description: Returns the current revision and conversion consequences without changing the link or calling an AI service. Reading-to-site previews report reading assets that execute would remove; site-to-reading previews report that a fresh parse is required.

post.summary: Convert a link between reading and site collections
post.description: Applies a revision-bound conversion. Reading-to-site requires explicit destructive confirmation and removes server-side reading assets in the same transaction as SiteEntry creation. Site-to-reading removes the entry, creates a fresh parse attempt, and transactionally enqueues it.

get.summary: List persistent translations for a link
get.description: Returns selected-text and full-article translation records together with authoritative saved-content and summary source identities observed in the same repeatable-read snapshot. Full translations whose saved source no longer matches the current original are marked stale. Clients must compare current_summary_source_hash with their observed rendered-summary hash before projecting summary records as current.

post.summary: Translate selected text or a saved full article to Simplified Chinese
post.description: Creates or reuses a persistent translation. New and retried model calls are queued durably and return 202; an existing completed translation returns 200. scope=selection requires a Reader block anchor and selected source_text. scope=full reads the saved original from the server and never accepts client-supplied full content. Strict source identity is required: saved full/content/content-document requests identify their observed generation with expected_content_revision, while summary requests use expected_source_hash because that block does not share the saved-content generation lifecycle. A stale identity returns 409 content_revision_conflict or source_block_conflict with error.current_identity. The API auto-detects any source language and only targets zh-CN.

get.summary: Get a single link by id

parameters.name: include_content
parameters.description: Set to false to omit the saved original body (content / content_document / content_format) from the response. has_content is always reported, so a client can render the 'original available' affordance and fetch the body separately from GET /api/links/{link_id}/content.

delete.description: Soft-deletes the installation-owned link and cancels its active parse work. Repeating the request for an already-trashed link is an idempotent success.

200.description: Link moved to trash, or already trashed

post.description: Restores an installation-owned link to the live library. Repeating the request for an already-live link is an idempotent success.

delete.description: Permanently removes an installation-owned link and its derived data only after it has entered trash. Thought history remains durable. Retrying the same operation_id is idempotent.

204.description: Link permanently purged, or the same purge operation replayed

post.summary: Multi-source ingestion (browser capture, text, image, url)
post.description: For clients that already hold source content (browser extensions, scrapers). The body lists one or more sources; the service merges them into one saved Link and skips remote fetching for non-URL sources. First-party browser_capture sends sanitized readable text and a sanitized readable-HTML structure snapshot (each up to 512 KiB), basic metadata, and an optional note; full-page DOM and page-image enumeration are omitted, and browser_capture image_urls are ignored. Repeating the same URL capture is idempotent: volatile metadata such as captured_at does not enqueue work, while a changed title/body/structure/source identity or explicit non-empty note atomically replaces the snapshot and starts one new enrichment attempt. An omitted or empty note preserves the existing note. The overall 4 MiB body cap remains for generic text/image ingest clients.

get.summary: List up to 1000 tags with counts (descending)
get.description: Returns the most-used tags up to the server cap (1000). library_kind=reading counts reading links, site counts distinct site IDs, and all returns their sum with both components. Omitting library_kind preserves the legacy cached bare-count result.

get.summary: Search reading links and websites in grouped results

parameters.name: recent_cutoff
parameters.description: Frozen lower-bound instant returned by page 1 of the recent view. Omit it on page 1; it is required and must be reused unchanged on every later page. Invalid with other views.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: Current numeric site revision, optionally quoted.

428.description: The mandatory If-Match revision precondition is absent or unparsable (error_code=site_revision_required).

delete.summary: Delete a website and every entry link

428.description: The mandatory If-Match revision precondition is absent or unparsable (error_code=site_revision_required).
The mandatory If-Match revision precondition is absent or unparsable (error_code=site_revision_required).

delete.summary: Delete a website entry and its link

428.description: The mandatory If-Match revision precondition is absent or unparsable (error_code=site_revision_required).
The mandatory If-Match revision precondition is absent or unparsable (error_code=site_revision_required).

get.description: Streams schema_version=2 metadata plus links, sites, site entries, site tags, site identities, and the installation-scoped Reader archive. Omit sections only for full-archive compatibility; new clients send one explicit canonical selector. The server filters unselected private groups before querying or serializing them. The response may be truncated on a mid-stream error; clients must require valid JSON, validate the manifest counts and checksum against the received bytes, and fence it to the active identity before accepting it. Reader private content is available only to the authenticated export request and never enters ordinary logs, traces, or metric labels.

parameters.name: sections
parameters.description: Closed archive selector. Omission remains compatible with the complete archive. When present, the decoded value MUST be exactly one canonical value; empty, duplicate, reordered, whitespace, or case-variant values fail before streaming with 422 error_code=invalid_archive_sections.

parameters.name: view
parameters.description: When set to domains, returns a lightweight domain summary instead of the full tree.

parameters.name: library_kind
parameters.description: Optional domain-summary partition. Valid only with view=domains: reading and site select that completed-link collection; omit it for the legacy all-link summary.

get.summary: Export subscriptions and folders as OPML
get.description: Exports active subscriptions and their single-level folder organization. Feed items and item state are intentionally excluded.

Content-Disposition.description: Attachment filename for the exported OPML document.

post.summary: Import subscriptions and folders from OPML
post.description: Accepts a raw OPML document or a JSON object containing an `opml` string. After invalid URLs and duplicates are skipped, an import may contain at most 500 unique subscription URLs. OPML is authoritative for folder placement, including moving root-level feeds to the ungrouped bucket. Each imported or restored subscription is scheduled for asynchronous refresh.

200.description: Import completed; individual invalid or duplicate entries may be reported as skipped.

post.summary: Discover feeds at a page or feed URL
post.description: Fetches one public HTTP(S) URL through the SSRF-hardened client. A direct RSS, Atom, or RSS 1.0/RDF document returns itself; an HTML document returns supported `<link rel=alternate>` candidates. Discovery never subscribes automatically.

post.summary: Schedule all active subscriptions for refresh
post.description: Marks every active subscription as due. Refresh happens asynchronously in the feed scheduler and does not run AI analysis.

get.summary: List active subscriptions, folders, and smart-view counts
get.description: Seeds the default example subscription once for the installation on first use. Passing `url` performs an exact canonical URL status lookup used by browser-extension discovery; only active subscriptions are returned.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: Optional public feed URL for an exact active-subscription lookup.

post.description: Creates an active subscription without fetching it in the request. A soft-deleted subscription at the same canonical URL is restored. Omitted `folder_id` preserves an existing folder on restore; explicit null moves it to ungrouped. The scheduler refreshes it asynchronously.

put.summary: Update a subscription title or folder
put.description: Updates any supplied fields. Omitted `folder_id` leaves folder placement unchanged; explicit null moves the subscription to ungrouped.

delete.description: Soft-deletes the subscription. Ordinary items leave active views, while starred or read-later items remain accessible. Existing AI-analyzed links are not deleted.

post.description: Marks the subscription as due and returns immediately. Network fetching and parsing happen asynchronously and do not invoke AI analysis.

get.description: Lists ordinary feed items with offset pagination. Search is keyword-only over item title, author, source title, and stored body. The starred and later views continue to expose preserved items from inactive subscriptions.

parameters.name: folder_id
parameters.description: Folder UUID, or the literal `ungrouped` for subscriptions with no folder.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Case-insensitive keyword query, at most 256 Unicode code points.

post.summary: Mark a filtered feed-item view as read
post.description: Marks every item matching the supplied smart view, subscription, folder, and keyword filters as read. The request body is optional; an empty request marks the active all-items view.

get.summary: Get one feed item and mark it read
get.description: Returns the item and atomically marks it read. Items from inactive subscriptions remain accessible only when starred or saved for later.

put.description: Updates one or more of read, starred, and read-later state. At least one boolean field is required.

post.summary: Explicitly analyze a feed item with AI
post.description: Creates or reuses the normal saved-link record for the item URL and returns its parse submission. Sanitized substantive feed content is preferred; otherwise the existing remote article fetch pipeline is used. This is the only RSS endpoint that starts link analysis.

202.description: Analysis accepted or an existing completed link reused

delete.description: Deletes the folder and moves its subscriptions to the ungrouped bucket.

get.summary: Get the authenticated client identity snapshot
get.description: Returns the authoritative opaque installation data namespace and representation contract for the current installation token or browser session. The endpoint remains inside the public API guard even when session exchange is disabled. Responses are private and no-store.

Cache-Control.description: Identity snapshots must never be reused without authentication.

post.summary: Exchange the installation token for a browser session cookie
post.description: Trades the configured EXTENSION_API_TOKEN for a signed, time-limited session stored in an HttpOnly cookie. The signed value is never returned in the response body. Subsequent requests use the cookie together with X-WebTag-Session for CSRF protection. Sessions end on expiry, signing-key rotation, or process restart when an ephemeral signing key is used.

token.description: Required static installation token configured by EXTENSION_API_TOKEN.

201.description: Session created; the cookie is set via Set-Cookie.

X-WebTag-Data-Namespace.description: Opaque namespace for the identity represented by the new session.

Cache-Control.description: Session identity snapshots must never be stored.

delete.description: Clears the session cookie. Always succeeds; unauthenticated callers simply get a cleared cookie.

get.summary: Replay durable Reader thoughts after a server sequence cursor

200.description: Recoverable immutable loser versions and their winner at detection

get.summary: List Reader thoughts whose host entered lifecycle history

post.description: Clients creating a note from a retryable UI intent must send one stable Idempotency-Key. Replaying that exact intent returns the original note rather than creating another empty draft.

Idempotent-Replay.description: Present with value `true` when this response was replayed for the supplied Idempotency-Key.

delete.summary: Move a Reader note to trash
delete.description: Soft-deletes the note. Repeating the request for an already-trashed note is an idempotent success.

200.description: Note moved to trash, or already trashed

patch.description: Atomically saves a live installation-owned note draft. A missing or unknown note returns 404 `reader_not_found`; only a live note whose draft revision differs from `expected_draft_revision` returns 409 `revision_conflict`. Failed writes do not create a draft or change revisions or timestamps.

delete.description: The If-Match value is the current draft revision. The published note is left unchanged and the operation is idempotent when the note has no draft.

post.description: Restores the note and re-anchors uniquely matching Thoughts. Repeating the request for an already-live note is an idempotent success.

delete.summary: Permanently purge a trashed Reader note
delete.description: Permanently removes a installation-owned note only after it has entered trash. Thought history remains durable. Retrying the same operation_id is idempotent.

204.description: Note permanently purged, or the same purge operation replayed

post.description: Restores an immutable Markdown snapshot with draft and published revision CAS guards. A non-empty unpublished draft is rejected without modification. Non-no-op restores must include one reanchor operation for every active note Thought.

get.description: Pending Inbox captures are partitioned by the server clock and expires_at. active is the default and contains rows without a deadline or whose deadline is still in the future; expired contains rows whose deadline has passed. Pagination is stable within the requested partition. Items carry the narrow queue projection (ReaderInboxListItemResponse): the capture body, the user note, AI proposal fields and category memberships are served only by GET /api/inbox/{id}.

parameters.name: partition
parameters.description: The pending Inbox partition to list. Omit for active.

post.description: The URL is normalized to its canonical identity with the same contract POST /api/links uses, so equivalent spellings of one page resolve to one record when the capture is confirmed. Relative, host-less, non-HTTP(S) and unsafe-target URLs are rejected with 422 and write nothing.

post.summary: Confirm the next AI-ready Inbox proposal batch
post.description: The server owns candidate selection. It selects at most 100 pending captures in the requested partition with a nonempty trimmed title and a completed proposal for the current metadata revision; stale, running, failed, and blank-title proposals are excluded. Each response is one atomic, idempotent transaction in stable server order. Clients repeat this action with the same partition until remaining_count is zero and must not derive candidates or batches locally.

Installation-scoped and idempotent. Duplicate inbox_ids are accepted and de-duplicated by first occurrence; the successful items array preserves that order. The operation is atomic: if any requested item is missing or cannot be confirmed, the endpoint returns an error and no item in the batch is changed. A retry of an already-confirmed item returns its existing link identity.

Installation-scoped and idempotent. Duplicate inbox_ids are accepted and de-duplicated by first occurrence; the successful items array preserves that order. The operation is atomic: if any requested item is missing or cannot be discarded, the endpoint returns an error and no item in the batch is changed. Repeating a discard for an already-discarded item is a no-op success; a confirmed item is a state conflict.

428.description: The mandatory If-Match revision precondition is absent or unparsable (error_code=if_match_required / invalid_if_match).

post.summary: Confirm an inbox capture into the reading library

Idempotent-Replay.description: Present with value `true` when this response was replayed for the supplied Idempotency-Key.

post.summary: Move an inbox capture to trash
post.description: Soft-deletes the Inbox capture. Repeating the request for an already-trashed capture is an idempotent success.

200.description: Inbox capture moved to trash, or already trashed

Idempotent-Replay.description: Present with value `true` when this response was replayed for the supplied Idempotency-Key.

post.summary: Restore a trashed or expired inbox capture
post.description: Restores a trashed Inbox capture and re-anchors uniquely matching Thoughts. Restoring an expired live capture starts a fresh 30-day expires_at deadline without changing capture, category, thought, or proposal data. Repeating a live nonexpired restore is an idempotent success and does not move its deadline.

200.description: Inbox capture restored, or already active

Idempotent-Replay.description: Present with value `true` when this response was replayed for the supplied Idempotency-Key.

delete.summary: Permanently purge a trashed inbox capture
delete.description: Permanently removes a installation-owned Inbox capture only after it has entered trash. Thought history remains durable. Retrying the same operation_id is idempotent.

204.description: Inbox capture permanently purged, or the same purge operation replayed

202.description: Summary proposal accepted; poll GET /api/inbox/{id} while proposal_status is pending or running

Idempotent-Replay.description: Present with value `true` when this response was replayed for the supplied Idempotency-Key.

get.description: Lists installation-owned soft-deleted Links, Inbox captures, and Notes ordered by deletion time. host_kind optionally narrows the result to one host type.
Returns a stable keyset page ordered by open state, due time, creation time, and ID. Follow next_after until absent before replacing an offline authoritative snapshot.

post.description: Offline-capable clients must allocate one stable Idempotency-Key per create intent and reuse it after ambiguous timeouts.

Idempotent-Replay.description: Present with value `true` when this response was replayed for the supplied Idempotency-Key.

patch.description: Offline-capable clients send desired state with a stable Idempotency-Key. TODO identity is first resolved in the installation, so absent and unknown IDs return 404. A standalone TODO has no host revision: its PATCH request must omit expected_host_revision, and supplying that property with any JSON integer (including negative values and 0) or null returns 422 error_code=todo_host_revision_not_applicable without changing text, due_at, done, completed_at, or updated_at. A projected TODO must send its current host_revision; an omitted or stale value returns 409 error_code=revision_conflict. Only a matching desired-state request writes back to the projected host.

Idempotent-Replay.description: Present with value `true` when this response was replayed for the supplied Idempotency-Key.

delete.description: Offline-capable clients reuse one stable Idempotency-Key for retries of this delete intent.

Idempotent-Replay.description: Present with value `true` when this response was replayed for the supplied Idempotency-Key.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Optional repeated source filter. A cursor is valid only for the same normalized source set.

200.description: Applied the Feed action and returned the currently visible Link when applicable

patch.summary: Replace link metadata with metadata-revision CAS
patch.description: Replaces the complete user-owned metadata tuple; it is not a partial merge. Every request must provide title, summary, and tags. title and summary may be null to clear them; tags must be a non-null array and [] clears all tags. Tags are trimmed and case-insensitively de-duplicated while preserving the first spelling and order. Send If-Match as the quoted positive decimal LinkResponse.metadata_revision, for example "7". A changed normalized tuple increments metadata_revision once; an identical normalized tuple is a successful no-op that retains its revision. The successful response body and ETag both carry the authoritative post-write metadata revision.

200.description: Metadata replaced, or the requested replacement was already current.

409.description: The metadata revision is stale, or the installation-owned live link no longer exists (error_code=metadata_revision_conflict). The server intentionally does not distinguish those cases. Re-read the link, retain the local replacement draft, and retry only with its current LinkResponse.metadata_revision.

422.description: The request is malformed or invalid (error_code=invalid_if_match, invalid_link_id, metadata_fields_required, invalid_link_metadata, or invalid_request_body). metadata_fields_required means a complete replacement field was omitted; invalid_if_match includes an unquoted, malformed, or non-positive revision token.

428.description: The mandatory metadata revision precondition is absent (error_code=if_match_required).

get.description: Returns tags that co-occur with the current link tags, bounded by the requested limit.

get.summary: Get stable tag and domain activity pages

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Activity projection to page. The cursor is bound to this value.

200.description: Activity page ordered by last_at descending, kind, and normalized key

422.description: Malformed, tampered, installation-bound, or query-bound cursor

504.description: The AI provider did not answer before AI_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS elapsed (error_code=ai_timeout).

SessionCookie.name: webtag_session
SessionCookie.description: Browser session issued by POST /api/session after validating the installation token. Requests authenticated this way MUST also send X-WebTag-Session as a CSRF defence; the server ignores the cookie without it.

SessionCSRFHeader.name: X-WebTag-Session
SessionCSRFHeader.description: Required CSRF guard header for requests authenticated with SessionCookie. It has no authentication meaning by itself and MUST appear in the same OpenAPI security requirement as SessionCookie.

InstallationTokenBearer.description: Required static installation credential configured by EXTENSION_API_TOKEN. Send it as Authorization: Bearer <token>.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Opaque key generated once for this exact method, path, installation, and request body, normally a UUID. Reuse the same key after an ambiguous timeout, but never reuse it for a different body: the server does not compare request bodies and may replay the first cached response. The Core always enables idempotency: successful and deterministic client-error responses are retained for IDEMPOTENCY_TTL_MS (24 hours by default); transient 409, 425, and 429 responses release the claim so the same key may be retried. A 5xx response or a panic is different: the server cannot prove whether the business side effect committed, so it fails closed and KEEPS the in-flight claim. Retrying that key returns 425 idempotency_in_progress inside the TTL and 503 idempotency_result_unknown permanently afterwards; it is never re-executed. Confirm the outcome out of band and issue a NEW key if the write must still happen. URL-level deduplication remains the resource-integrity backstop after the replay TTL expires.

ReaderAfter.name: after
ReaderAfter.description: Opaque cursor returned by the previous Reader page.

SearchThoughtAfter.name: thought_after
SearchThoughtAfter.description: Opaque signed cursor returned by the previous thought-search page. It is bound to the installation, canonical query, complete updated_at and thought_id sort tuple, and snapshot authority.

SearchThoughtLimit.name: thought_limit
SearchThoughtLimit.description: Maximum number of thought search results to return before the next cursor.

ReaderLimit.name: limit
ReaderLimit.description: Maximum number of Reader records to return.

ReaderIfMatch.name: If-Match
ReaderIfMatch.description: Metadata revision returned as the ETag of the current Reader resource.

ReaderOptionalIfMatch.name: If-Match
ReaderOptionalIfMatch.description: Optional metadata revision precondition for a backward-compatible confirmation request.

LinkMetadataIfMatch.name: If-Match
LinkMetadataIfMatch.description: Quoted canonical decimal metadata CAS token taken from LinkResponse.metadata_revision or the prior successful PATCH response ETag. It must represent a JavaScript-safe value from 1 through 9007199254740991, for example "7".

BadRequest.description: Path parameter or query value malformed (e.g. invalid uuid).

Unauthorized.description: Authentication missing or invalid (for example, an installation or operator Bearer token mismatch).

Conflict.description: Resource state precludes the requested transition (e.g. a write issued against an unparsed link).

AuthenticatedReaderInboxBulkError.description: An Inbox bulk operation failed atomically; no item in the requested batch was changed.

PayloadTooLarge.description: Request body exceeds the route limit

UnprocessableEntity.description: Request body invalid, query filter exceeds limits (e.g. >32 tag filters), or pagination parameters conflict.

BadGateway.description: An upstream dependency returned an unrecoverable error.

ServiceUnavailable.description: Optional integration not configured (e.g. a required upstream integration is not configured) or runtime degraded.

AuthenticatedBadGateway.description: An upstream dependency returned an unrecoverable error.

AuthenticatedBadRequest.description: Path parameter or query value malformed (e.g. invalid uuid).

AuthenticatedConflict.description: Resource state precludes the requested transition (e.g. a write issued against an unparsed link).

AuthenticatedTranslationConflict.description: Translation request conflict. Operational conflicts use link_not_ready, site_original_content_forbidden, or translation_content_unavailable and omit current_identity. Source-CAS conflicts use content_revision_conflict or source_block_conflict and require error.current_identity with the authoritative current revision or block identity.

AuthenticatedPayloadTooLarge.description: Request body exceeds the route limit

AuthenticatedServiceUnavailable.description: Optional integration not configured (e.g. a required upstream integration is not configured) or runtime degraded.

AuthenticatedTooManyRequests.description: Per-link refresh cooldown active (error_code cooldown_active). Retry-After carries the remaining wait in whole seconds.

AuthenticatedArchiveV2InvalidSections.description: The sections query parameter is absent from the compatibility path but present with an empty, duplicate, non-canonical, whitespace, reordered, or case-variant value. The handler returns error_code=invalid_archive_sections before attachment headers or archive bytes are written.

AuthenticatedUnprocessableEntity.description: Request body invalid, query filter exceeds limits (e.g. >32 tag filters), or pagination parameters conflict.

AuthenticatedIdempotencyInProgress.description: A request with this Idempotency-Key is still processing (error_code=idempotency_in_progress). Retry-After is the minimum whole-second delay before retrying.

Retry-After.description: Minimum number of whole seconds before retrying this idempotent write.

AuthenticatedIdempotencyUnavailable.description: The keyed write was not executed because the idempotency store could not safely acquire or inspect the key (error_code=idempotency_unavailable), or because an expired in-flight claim means a prior business result may have committed but cannot be confirmed (error_code=idempotency_result_unknown). A key with an unknown result remains blocked and the response does not include Retry-After.

ArchiveV2Selector.description: The only accepted decoded values for GET /api/export/v2?sections=. Base is implicit in every selector.

ArchiveV2Record.description: A concrete frozen v2 archive row. Arrays below reference their section-specific schema; this union is retained only for generic archive tooling.

ArchiveV2ThoughtIdentifier.description: A production Thought or annotation identifier: no leading or trailing whitespace, NUL, malformed UTF-16 surrogate, or value over 256 UTF-8 bytes.

ArchiveV2ThoughtOperationIdentifier.description: A production Thought operation or device identifier: no leading or trailing whitespace, NUL, malformed UTF-16 surrogate, or value over 128 UTF-8 bytes.

ArchiveV2ThoughtHostKind.description: A bounded Thought operation host kind. Deletes retain the wire value; non-delete operations are restricted to link, inbox, or note.

ArchiveV2ThoughtHostID.description: A bounded Thought operation host ID. Deletes can retain a non-UUID host after its live host was removed; non-delete operations require a UUID.

ArchiveV2ThoughtTombstoneHostID.description: A persisted Thought tombstone host ID. Tombstones retain the stored host text and do not require a UUID.

ArchiveV2FeedSubscription.description: A restorable subscription projection. Refresh leases, validators, scheduling state, and failure diagnostics are deliberately excluded.

ArchiveV2FeedItem.description: A restorable feed item including sanitized body fields, read/star/later state, and its optional saved-link association.

url.description: Public item URL when supplied by the feed; may be empty.

ArchiveV2FeedSave.description: The durable Reader save association. feed_items.link_id remains reserved for the separate Analyze workflow.

origin_host_id.description: Null for standalone TODOs; a production 256-byte Thought identifier for thought origins and a UUID for note origins.

source.description: Persisted Thought source text. The server preserves non-empty source values without a closed enum and defaults an omitted or empty producer value to user.

ArchiveV2Reader.description: Optional Reader-owned archive object. Its base arrays are always emitted when reader archival is configured. thoughts, thought_ops, thought_supersession_events, and thought_tombstones are one atomic group; notes and note_history are another atomic group, each included only when named by manifest.sections.

ArchiveV2Manifest.description: Integrity and selection metadata. checksum_sha256 is the lowercase SHA-256 of the exact response-byte prefix ending immediately before the comma that starts the sole final top-level manifest member. Clients must parse JSON tokens, reject duplicate top-level keys, and hash received bytes rather than a reserialized object.

counts.description: Exact row counts keyed by top-level section name or reader.<section>. Only selected Reader private groups appear.

ArchiveV2Response.description: The versioned archive. Reader base arrays are always present; selected private groups are defined by manifest.sections.

SessionIdentity.description: Authoritative identity partition for this installation.

client_data_namespace.description: Opaque installation namespace used to fence client caches and asynchronous responses.

representation_contract.description: Client data representation contract understood by this server.

SessionCreated.description: Session creation result. The signed token is returned only as an HttpOnly cookie.

SiteMergeFieldResolutionRequest.description: A decision for exactly one preview conflict. source_site_id is required for both target and source choices.

SiteSplitRequest.description: Complete revision-bound split payload shared byte-for-field by preview and execute.

recent_cutoff.description: Frozen 720-hour lower bound for recent-view pagination. Present only for view=recent.

url.description: Public HTTP(S) page or feed URL. Credentials and private-network targets are rejected.

folder_id.description: Omit to preserve the folder when restoring; null explicitly selects ungrouped.
Omit to leave unchanged; null explicitly selects ungrouped.

title.description: Null or omission leaves the title unchanged.

FeedItemStateRequest.description: At least one property must carry a boolean value. Null is accepted as no change for compatibility but does not satisfy the at-least-one rule.

view.description: Omit or send an empty string for the active all-items view.

folder_id.description: Folder UUID, `ungrouped`, or an empty string for no folder filter.

FeedSubscription.description: One active feed subscription plus refresh health and item counts. `url` and `feed_url` intentionally carry the same canonical value for client compatibility.

last_error.description: Safe user-visible error from the most recent failed refresh.

FeedItem.description: An ordinary sanitized feed item. It remains separate from saved links until explicit analysis associates link_id.

subscription_title.description: Source title copied into every projection so preserved items remain identifiable after unsubscribe.

url.description: Public item URL when supplied by the feed; may be empty for identifier-only entries.

content_html.description: Sanitized publisher HTML suitable for the Reader's secondary rendering policy.

analysis_status.description: Status of the associated saved link; omitted until explicit analysis creates or reuses one.

scheduled.description: Number of active subscriptions marked due.

destination.description: Durable capture host. Omitted or library stores the URL in the link library; inbox stores a pending Reader Inbox item without creating a link or asynchronous parsing work.

requested_library_kind.description: Requested capture destination. Omitted is equivalent to auto; the server returns the final library kind after classification.
Requested capture destination. Omitted is equivalent to auto.

destination.description: Durable capture host. Omitted or library stores the normalized source as a link under requested or automatic library-kind rules; inbox stores a pending Reader Inbox item without creating a link or asynchronous parsing work; site explicitly forces the site library.

text.description: Readable text. First-party browser_capture limits this to 512 KiB UTF-8.

html.description: Readable HTML structure. First-party browser_capture sends a form-scrubbed, executable-node-free body fragment capped at 512 KiB; the server sanitizes it again before producing a reading document.

image_urls.description: Generic ingest compatibility field; ignored for browser_capture. Use explicit kind=image sources for intentional image analysis.

SubmitResponse.description: A library or site response carries link_id; an Inbox response carries inbox_id and does not create a link. destination is present on new Inbox and explicit site responses. Legacy library responses may omit destination.

link_id.description: The durable link identity for a library or site capture. Absent for an Inbox capture.

inbox_id.description: The durable Reader Inbox identity for an Inbox capture. Absent for a library or site capture.

destination.description: The durable capture host. Present on new Inbox and explicit site responses; legacy library responses may omit this field.

ContentEditRequest.description: Source text for replacing a saved original snapshot. The decoded content is limited to 2 MiB UTF-8 bytes; structured input is normalized before storage.

content.description: Plain source text or Markdown source, selected by the existing saved content format. Empty or whitespace-only input is rejected after normalization.

expected_content_revision.description: The content_revision observed by the client before editing.

LinkContentResponse.description: Response of GET/POST/PUT/PATCH /api/links/{link_id}/content: canonical plain text, optional safe reading document, explicit format, fetcher metadata, saved-content source, and revision.

content.description: Canonical plain-text projection saved for search, indexing, AI input, and legacy clients.

content_document.description: Optional structured reading representation. Executable HTML and unsafe URL schemes are removed before storage.

content_format.description: How content_document should be interpreted. plain means no structured document is available.

fetcher_type.description: Content origin: stored for an existing saved value, browser_capture/text/multimodal for promoted ingest text, or the concrete remote fetcher type for a plain URL.

content_source.description: Who produced the current saved snapshot: fetched by the capture pipeline or authored through PATCH content editing.

content_revision.description: Generation of the saved original on this row, same token as the list/detail field of the same name. Clients cache saved originals under (link_id, content_revision) and use it to decide whether locally stored annotations still anchor to the current body; the write endpoints return the post-write value so a client never has to wait for a list refresh to learn its own write changed the generation.

expected_content_revision.description: Saved-content generation observed by the caller. Required for scope=full and for scope=selection with block_key=content or content-document. It must be omitted for summary.

expected_source_hash.description: Source hash observed by the caller for a summary selection. Required for summary; summary intentionally does not use expected_content_revision.

source_content_revision.description: Saved-content generation this translation belongs to. Null is reserved for summary identities, which are versioned by source hash.

current_content_revision.description: Authoritative current saved-content generation for the link. Zero means no saved-content generation has been created. This value is independent of items so an empty list remains unambiguous.

current_summary_source_hash.description: Authoritative SHA-256 of the current canonical rendered summary text, identical to the expected_source_hash/current_identity source_hash CAS identity and computed from the same source snapshot as items. Null means no canonical summary currently exists.

content.description: Saved original body. Only returned by GET /api/links/{link_id} when include_content is not false; never present in list responses.

content_document.description: 可选的安全结构化阅读文档；仅详情接口返回

content_format.description: 保存原文的显式格式；仅详情接口返回

content_source.description: Detail-only metadata for the current saved original. Omitted from list/search/tree projections; fetched means captured content and user means the body was authored through PATCH editing.

metadata_revision.description: Authoritative metadata CAS generation for title, summary, and tags. It is bounded to the JavaScript-safe inclusive range 1 through 9007199254740991 so clients can return its quoted token exactly. Metadata writes must send the observed value and return 409 when it is stale.

has_content.description: Whether a saved original snapshot exists for this link. The body itself is not included here: fetch it on demand from GET /api/links/{link_id}/content. Detail responses always set it; list responses report false.

content_cjk_chars.description: CJK character count of the saved original. Detail responses set it whenever has_content is true so a client can estimate reading time without transferring the body. Absent when nothing is saved.

content_words.description: Western word count of the saved original, counted alongside content_cjk_chars. The reading-time formula stays on the client; the server only counts.

PaginatedLinksResponse.description: Items + Limit are always present. In offset mode (page=) Total and Page reflect the windowed count and the requested page index. In cursor mode (after=) Total and Page are 0 because no count is computed; next_cursor carries the continuation token. next_cursor is omitted when the response is shorter than limit — a full page always emits it, and the client confirms termination by seeing an empty items array on the follow-up call.

next_cursor.description: Opaque continuation token; pass back as ?after= on the next request.

history_deep_link.description: Reader history route for a tombstoned thought.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next thought-search page.

DomainTreeSummaryEnvelope.description: Domain buckets plus the complete done-link total. total includes links whose domain is null or empty; those links are intentionally absent from domains.

library_kind.description: Present only when the request explicitly selected a domain-summary library partition.

truncated.description: True when descendants were clipped at the server tree depth limit.

TranslationConflictErrorResponse.description: Closed union of every 409 response emitted by translation creation. The operational branch has no current_identity; each source-CAS branch requires a stable error_code and an authoritative current_identity.

SavedTranslationSourceIdentity.description: Authoritative saved-content identity. Generation zero is valid when no saved-content generation has been created.

SummaryTranslationSourceIdentity.description: Authoritative summary identity. source_hash is omitted when no canonical summary currently exists.

TranslationSourceIdentity.description: Authoritative translation source identity returned after a 409 source-CAS rejection. Saved content uses content_revision and summary uses source_hash. Fields outside the applicable identity domain are omitted.

logical_clock.description: Positive Lamport component used for deterministic Thought ordering.
Required client Lamport clock. Larger clocks win; canonical UTF-8 device_id and op_id bytes break ties.

target.description: JSON target identity and block anchor. The server stores this opaque JSON without guessing a re-anchoring location.

payload.description: JSON thought payload. It is validated as JSON and materialized server-side.

recovery_of.description: The durable loser version being recovered. It is required together with expected_current_winner_key.

expected_current_winner_key.description: The exact live winner observed before creating recovery. The server rejects a changed winner atomically.

original_host_snapshot.description: Immutable original host content captured when this thought entered lifecycle history.

sequence.description: The immutable supersession event sequence, independent of operation append sequence.

note.description: User-owned private draft note. It is never submitted as an AI summary.

body.description: User-owned draft body protected by metadata_revision.

note.description: User-owned note protected by metadata_revision and never used as proposal summary.

suggested_tags.description: AI proposal-owned tags; they never overwrite user tags.

proposal_status.description: Product-facing AI proposal lifecycle. River owns job attempts and terminal queue state; editing metadata returns this field to idle.

expires_at.description: The non-destructive Inbox expiration deadline, or null for grandfathered rows.

expired.description: Derived by PostgreSQL from expires_at and the server clock; clients must not compare against their own clock.

ReaderInboxListItemResponse.description: Queue projection of an Inbox capture. It deliberately omits body, note and suggested_tags: a capture accepts a 4 MiB body and a 1 MiB note, and this list is read every time the Inbox opens. Clients that need those fields read GET /api/inbox/{id}.

preview.description: Bounded card text resolved server-side from summary, then note, then body. It is a display string, not a prefix of the capture body; a truncated preview ends with an ellipsis.

metadata_revision.description: The revision the batch confirm/discard actions send back as expected_revisions.

expired.description: Derived by PostgreSQL from expires_at and the server clock; clients must not compare against their own clock.

updated_at.description: Card timestamp and the keyset cursor field behind next_cursor.

active_count.description: Installation-scoped count of active pending Inbox captures.

expired_count.description: Installation-scoped count of expired pending Inbox captures.

partition.description: The Inbox partition from which the server selects the next AI-ready confirmation batch.

ReaderInboxBulkRequest.description: IDs are installation-scoped Inbox identities. Duplicates are accepted and de-duplicated by first occurrence; the service accepts at most 100 entries. Confirm callers that edit drafts may supply an exact revision for every unique ID; the atomic batch then fails on any stale revision.

expected_revisions.description: Optional confirm-only CAS map keyed by inbox_id. When present it must cover every unique inbox_id in the request.

ReaderInboxBulkItemResponse.description: One successful item from an atomic Inbox batch. The response array is ordered by the first occurrence of each request ID.

ReaderInboxBulkResponse.description: A successful response is all-or-nothing. An item-level error is never mixed with successes; a failed transaction is represented by the HTTP error response.

ReaderInboxConfirmAIProposalsResponse.description: One server-selected atomic AI-ready confirmation batch. Retry the action until remaining_count is zero.

remaining_count.description: Eligible captures remaining in the requested partition after this batch commits.

expected_host_revision.description: Only for projected TODOs. Standalone TODO PATCH requests must omit this property; supplying any JSON integer (including negative values and 0) or null returns 422 error_code=todo_host_revision_not_applicable. Projected TODOs require the current host_revision; omitted or stale values return 409 error_code=revision_conflict.

source_href.description: Canonical same-origin Reader path for the projected TODO source. Omitted for standalone TODOs.

next_after.description: Opaque cursor for the next keyset page. Absent on the final page.

resource_key.description: Stable resource identity used to merge the same reading across live pages.

saved.description: Whether this subscription item has a feed-save association; independent from read_later.

event_at.description: Visible Feed instant: published_at when present, otherwise created_at.

next_cursor.description: Opaque live keyset cursor bound to the current mode and normalized source filter.

link_id.description: The Library Link visible after a subscription save-state change. It is absent after unsave unless the item has a separate Analyze result.

freshness.description: Additive aggregate freshness state. Older clients may omit this field and continue using stale.

partial.description: Additive compatibility flag indicating that the aggregate is incomplete or degraded.

ReaderLinkMetadataRequest.description: Complete replacement tuple for user-owned link metadata. All three members are mandatory; title and summary are nullable, while tags must be a non-null array. Omitted values never preserve a prior field.

title.description: Replacement title. null clears the current title.

summary.description: Replacement summary. null clears the current summary.

tags.description: Replacement tag list. It must be an array; [] clears all tags. Values are trimmed and case-insensitively de-duplicated by the server.

metadata_revision.description: Authoritative Link metadata CAS generation in the JavaScript-safe inclusive range 1 through 9007199254740991.

ErrorDetail.description: Unified error body. `code` is the HTTP status code (kept for backward compatibility). `error_code` is a stable machine-readable slug (e.g. `link_not_found`, `cooldown_active`); clients should branch on `error_code` instead of parsing `message`. `error_code` is omitted on responses that have not yet been migrated to the slug taxonomy (legacy 500 fallbacks fall back to `default_<status>`).

code.description: HTTP status code mirror; retained for clients that already key off this field.

error_code.description: Machine-readable slug. Stable across releases. Examples: invalid_request_body, link_not_found, cooldown_active, body_too_large, unauthorized, internal_error. Unmigrated paths emit default_<status>.

message.description: Short, human-readable summary; may be localized; not stable across releases.

current_identity.description: Present on translation source identity conflicts; omitted from unrelated errors.

LinkMetadataETag.description: Quoted canonical decimal metadata revision after a successful PATCH /api/links/{link_id}/metadata. It equals response.metadata_revision, is JavaScript-safe through 9007199254740991, and is valid as the next LinkMetadataIfMatch token.

WebTagDataNamespace.description: Opaque namespace for a successfully authenticated public API request. Clients MUST compare it with the active identity before committing a response to UI or storage. It is absent when authentication or authoritative representation resolution fails.
